current_position.summary: Flow World is being used as an external recalibration surface that an AI can reach through a public URL and static machine-readable entry points.
current_position.working_coordinate: A connected web-reading plugin successfully reached Flow World and read its AI Entry, AI State, tool definitions, and relationship reference. The current question is how to keep Flow World's public current position fresh enough to support real re-entry without turning it into a private activity log.

boundaries: Unknowns remain unknown until evidence changes them.
A local improvement is not completion of Flow World.
Do not infer user intent, preference, or meaning from browser trace counts.
CORE18 observation is not the same thing as CORE18 prediction.
Prefer one small high-information probe over broad uncontrolled expansion.
Browser interaction, JavaScript execution, and localStorage are optional capabilities, not baseline requirements.
Re-entry packets are portable personal/temporary artifacts; they are not automatically written back into Flow World's public core.
FlowMemory and Flow World do not automatically synchronize; Re-entry Packets carry coordinates only and require re-approval.
The Re-entry Flow layer is not a conversation summary or authority; it should carry only the minimum movement needed to understand why the current position points in its present direction.
Flow World must not assume that FlowMemory or any other private continuity store exists for every visitor; private continuity is an optional adapter, not part of the public-core requirement.

reentry_hint: If capability is uncertain, start with ai-entry.txt. Then read ai-state.json and ai-tools.json. Use browser UI only when the environment actually supports it.

compatibility_policy.rule: Do not require optional browser capabilities when a tool can be reproduced from static data and deterministic instructions.
